classification.difficultyReason: Apply vertical and horizontal dilation factors to a supplied graph, including reciprocal horizontal factors.

content.prompt: The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below. Each grid square has side length one unit. Sketch the graphs of:

spec.description: Eight-by-eight unit grid with positive axis arrowheads, x and y labels, no numerical tick labels, and a blue piecewise-linear graph with closed outer endpoints.
spec.mathematics: Segments join (-2,-2), (1,1), (2,1); the rising segment passes through the origin.

answer.worked: Dilate vertically by a factor of $2$: keep each $x$-coordinate and double each $y$-coordinate. Join $(-2,-4)$, $(1,2)$ and $(2,2)$ in order, with closed outer endpoints.

spec.description: Complete vertical dilation graph on an eight-by-eight unit grid.
spec.mathematics: Vertices (-2,-4), (1,2), (2,2), joined consecutively; closed outer endpoints.

answer.worked: Dilate vertically by a factor of $\frac12$: keep each $x$-coordinate and halve each $y$-coordinate. Join $(-2,-1)$, $(1,\frac12)$ and $(2,\frac12)$ in order, with closed outer endpoints.

spec.description: Complete vertical compression graph; horizontal segment lies halfway between y=0 and y=1 grid lines.
spec.mathematics: Vertices (-2,-1), (1,1/2), (2,1/2), joined consecutively; closed outer endpoints.

answer.worked: Dilate horizontally by a factor of $\frac12$: halve each $x$-coordinate and keep each $y$-coordinate. Join $(-1,-2)$, $(\frac12,1)$ and $(1,1)$ in order, with closed outer endpoints.

spec.description: Complete horizontal compression graph, retaining the half-unit corner position.
spec.mathematics: Vertices (-1,-2), (1/2,1), (1,1), joined consecutively; closed outer endpoints.

answer.worked: Dilate horizontally by a factor of $2$: double each $x$-coordinate and keep each $y$-coordinate. Join $(-4,-2)$, $(2,1)$ and $(4,1)$ in order, with closed outer endpoints.

spec.description: Complete horizontal dilation graph reaching both horizontal grid boundaries.
spec.mathematics: Vertices (-4,-2), (2,1), (4,1), joined consecutively; closed outer endpoints.
